data.note:
My call of Microtubule stabilizers was wrong; true annotation is Microtubule destabilizers.

What misled me: NSC vote was 4/4 stabilizer across 0.1-3 uM and 9/10 neighbors were reference stabilizers. I treated that as a strong prior and discounted the mechanistic clues pointing the other way: tub_mean z ~ -9 at 0.3 and 3 uM with diffuse dimmer tubulin noted by the microscopist, i.e. loss of microtubule mass, plus irregular lobed/fragmented nuclei, low solidity, and multinucleation - all classic failed cytokinesis/mitotic defect shared by both stabilizers and destabilizers.

Reflection: both classes arrest mitosis and produce large/multilobed nuclei and relative actin dominance, so image-embedding similarity alone does not separate them, especially at modest similarities 0.42-0.69. I should have weighted the direction of the tubulin feature and requested a discriminating tubulin-polymerization test as I listed in the follow-up.

Literature context: destabilizing agents acting at the colchicine site of tubulin are described as microtubule destabilizers (PMID:28640209); general tubulin/microtubule regulation by Op18/stathmin (PMID:10491392) and its phosphorylation regulated by assembly state (PMID:11179426) illustrate why stabilizers vs destabilizers can show overlapping mitotic-failure phenotypes, also seen where mitotic death can be independent of net polymerization (PMID:18485433).

reflection.text:
I over-weighted the reference atlas and under-weighted the visual and directional tubulin evidence. The NSC vote was 4/4 for Microtubule stabilizers with 9/10 k-neighbours as stabilizers (e5, e9, similarities 0.418-0.692), and I raised stabilizers from 0.50 to 0.65 despite non-significant dose-responses (rho +0.40 to -0.40, all p=0.6, e10-e12). That consistency across 0.1-3 uM felt confirmatory but was from only 4 wells in a narrow high-dose window with no low-dose anchor.

The measurements themselves were ambiguous in a way I misread. Very high act_tub_ratio (z=+20.1 to +44.3 in e2, e3, e7, e8) with high act_mean and very low nuc_solidity/form_factor (z=-20 to -35) can reflect relative tubulin loss plus distorted mitotic nuclei, not stabilization. The microscopist explicitly kept Microtubule destabilizers and Aurora kinase inhibitors as candidates with lower density (e4), and tub_mean trended down with dose (rho=-0.40, e11), directionally favoring destabilization, but I treated these as split alternatives rather than a warning that stabilizers and destabilizers converge on mitotic nuclear phenotypes.

The lesson is that NSC similarity on Cell Painting actin/tubulin balance does not separate stabilizer versus destabilizer when both disrupt mitosis, especially without a polymerization-direction assay. Future runs should not increase confidence on p=0.6 trends and should require a functional tubulin readout before choosing between these two classes.
what_was_right: Kept mitotic mechanism open: describe_phenotype flagged Microtubule destabilizers alongside Aurora kinase inhibitors with lower density vs DMSO (e4), which included the true class.
Recorded strong nuclear shape defect (nuc_solidity z=-20.3 to -35.5, nuc_form_factor z=-24.2 in e2, e7, e8) consistent with antimitotic microtubule perturbation.
Measured tub_mean dose trend negative (Spearman rho=-0.40, e11), directionally consistent with tubulin loss rather than net stabilization, even though p=0.6 with only 4 wells.
what_was_wrong: Trusted NSC 4/4 votes and 9/10 stabilizer neighbours (e5, e9) as decisive, despite modest per-well similarities 0.418-0.692 and no destabilizer comparator analysis.
Misinterpreted very high act_tub_ratio (z=+20 to +44) and high act_mean (z=+19 to +23 in e2, e3, e8) as stabilizer-like instead of relative actin dominance from tubulin depolymerization.

Upweighted Microtubule stabilizers from 0.50 to 0.65 on non-significant dose-responses (all p=0.6, e10-e12) and narrow 0.1-3 uM sampling without low-dose or washout data to test reversibility/bundling.

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Microtubule destabilizers**.

## Reflection

I over-weighted the reference atlas and under-weighted the visual and directional tubulin evidence. The NSC vote was 4/4 for Microtubule stabilizers with 9/10 k-neighbours as stabilizers (e5, e9, similarities 0.418-0.692), and I raised stabilizers from 0.50 to 0.65 despite non-significant dose-responses (rho +0.40 to -0.40, all p=0.6, e10-e12). That consistency across 0.1-3 uM felt confirmatory but was from only 4 wells in a narrow high-dose window with no low-dose anchor.

The measurements themselves were ambiguous in a way I misread. Very high act_tub_ratio (z=+20.1 to +44.3 in e2, e3, e7, e8) with high act_mean and very low nuc_solidity/form_factor (z=-20 to -35) can reflect relative tubulin loss plus distorted mitotic nuclei, not stabilization. The microscopist explicitly kept Microtubule destabilizers and Aurora kinase inhibitors as candidates with lower density (e4), and tub_mean trended down with dose (rho=-0.40, e11), directionally favoring destabilization, but I treated these as split alternatives rather than a warning that stabilizers and destabilizers converge on mitotic nuclear phenotypes.

The lesson is that NSC similarity on Cell Painting actin/tubulin balance does not separate stabilizer versus destabilizer when both disrupt mitosis, especially without a polymerization-direction assay. Future runs should not increase confidence on p=0.6 trends and should require a functional tubulin readout before choosing between these two classes.

What was right:
- Kept mitotic mechanism open: describe_phenotype flagged Microtubule destabilizers alongside Aurora kinase inhibitors with lower density vs DMSO (e4), which included the true class.
- Recorded strong nuclear shape defect (nuc_solidity z=-20.3 to -35.5, nuc_form_factor z=-24.2 in e2, e7, e8) consistent with antimitotic microtubule perturbation.
- Measured tub_mean dose trend negative (Spearman rho=-0.40, e11), directionally consistent with tubulin loss rather than net stabilization, even though p=0.6 with only 4 wells.

What was wrong or missed:
- Trusted NSC 4/4 votes and 9/10 stabilizer neighbours (e5, e9) as decisive, despite modest per-well similarities 0.418-0.692 and no destabilizer comparator analysis.
- Misinterpreted very high act_tub_ratio (z=+20 to +44) and high act_mean (z=+19 to +23 in e2, e3, e8) as stabilizer-like instead of relative actin dominance from tubulin depolymerization.
- Upweighted Microtubule stabilizers from 0.50 to 0.65 on non-significant dose-responses (all p=0.6, e10-e12) and narrow 0.1-3 uM sampling without low-dose or washout data to test reversibility/bundling.

Proposed next experiment: Cell-free tubulin polymerization assay with nocodazole versus paclitaxel stabilizer and colchicine-site destabilizer controls, paired with high-resolution anti-tubulin spindle imaging and drug washout to test for net microtubule loss versus bundling/stabilization.
